_comment: Declared blind spots of the quality defence, as measured by scripts/quality_matrix.py.
This file is a registry, not a to-do list: tests/test_quality_matrix.py fails when the
measured set of holes differs from the set declared here, in EITHER direction. A new
blind spot therefore cannot land silently - it has to be written down with an exit
criterion first - and a hole that gets closed cannot stay here as decoration, because
an obsolete entry reads as an open one.
Fields: id = '<kind>:<name>' exactly as measured; opened = date the measurement found
it; exit = the concrete, checkable state that removes it; why = one line of context.
QUALITY_MATRIX.md must list every id in this file and no others.

holes.why: The fuzz harness links pyrs-json and that crate exports to_json_text / to_jsonc_text / to_json5_text, but the only JSON target is parse_json: a parse-only target cannot see a writer, so nothing fuzzes text -> node -> text for the JSON family.
holes.exit: fuzz/fuzz_targets/json_roundtrip.rs exists, appears in the fuzz.yml matrix, has fuzz/seeds/json_roundtrip/, and the replay tier runs it on pull requests.

holes.why: Same shape as the JSON gap: pyrs-toml has a writer and only a parse_toml target.
holes.exit: fuzz/fuzz_targets/toml_roundtrip.rs exists, appears in the fuzz.yml matrix, has fuzz/seeds/toml_roundtrip/, and the replay tier runs it on pull requests.

holes.why: No workflow sets PROPTEST_CASES, so every CI run uses proptest's default 256 cases. Three fmt_pbt writer properties (JSON, JSON5, TOML) are known to fail at 20,000 cases and are invisible at 256, which is why the case count cannot simply be raised: raising it would redden every PR until those three close.
holes.exit: A blocking CI job runs the property tier at an agreed elevated case count, which requires prop_json_writers_are_fixed_points, prop_json5_writer_is_fixed_point and prop_toml_writer_is_fixed_point to hold there first.
